title: Steatosis shapes prognosis-defining liver metastasis heterogeneity in CRC.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and opened every file in the paper's only data deposit, GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) series GSE292820: raw count table is 23,399 genes x exactly 6 mouse samples (CMT93 colorectal cancer spheroids, 3 vehicle/BSA vs 3 palmitate), plus a DESeq2 differential-expression table (23,399 rows, one contrast 'PA vs BSA'), a gene-set enrichment table and a column-description README. Also pulled NCBI summaries for BioProject PRJNA1241311 (same 6 mouse samples) and for GSE151165, the external human dataset the paper reanalyses: 30 human samples from a different 2021 study.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the human patient cohort (steatosis status, growth-pattern scoring, survival) comes from the abstract and the Nature press/news coverage only. The article is paywalled, has no PubMed Central record and no supplementary files retrievable through Europe PMC, so no patient-level table was seen. The spatial metabolite and spatial protein analyses mentioned in the abstract have no deposit I could find in GEO, BioProject, Zenodo or Dryad.

a1_downloadable.note: GEO series GSE292820 downloads freely without login (I fetched all four supplementary files, ~1.2 MB total). But the patient data behind the paper's actual claims is not deposited anywhere I could find.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: In the downloaded files the only label is the 6-sample treatment group (palmitate vs vehicle), encoded in column names, not a column. The interesting label, growth pattern of a liver metastasis (replacement vs encapsulated), appears in no deposited file from this paper.

a3_inputs_present.note: Gene counts with Ensembl mouse gene IDs and symbols are present in the file; no identifier lookups needed.

a4_units_stated.note: Raw sequencing counts and DESeq2 log2 fold-change / p-value / q-value columns are all documented in the included column-description README.

a5_enough_rows.note: KILLER. The deposit is 6 RNA-seq samples (3 vs 3) from one mouse cell line. Genes are features, not examples. The external human set the paper reuses, GSE151165, has only 30 samples. Far under the ~400 minimum.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small; fits in memory many times over.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO metadata says 6 samples and the count table has exactly 6 sample columns; the paper's patient counts could not be checked because the article is paywalled.

a8_label_provenance.note: The treatment label (200 micromolar palmitate vs vehicle) is an experimental condition set by the authors, not another model's output; it just has only 6 instances.

existing_models.name: Neural image compression deep-learning classifier for histopathological growth patterns of colorectal liver metastasis (BJS Open 2024, Erasmus MC cohort)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search result summary reports area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.93 in the development cohort and 0.95 on external validation, classifying desmoplastic versus non-desmoplastic growth pattern from whole-slide haematoxylin and eosin images; I read the search snippet and abstract listing, not the full paper.

existing_models.name: COFFEE-type transformer 'AI copilot' for growth-pattern diagnosis in resectable colorectal liver metastases (prospective study, PMC12626517)
existing_models.score_and_split: Prospective clinical evaluation of growth-pattern classification from whole-slide images; numbers not retrieved, only the search result title and summary.

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: No join rescues a 6-sample experiment; the only sensible use of this deposit is as a gene-level signature to score against other datasets, which is statistics, not a model.

honest_claim_h3: With this deposit a model could only claim 'palmitate changes gene expression in one mouse colorectal cancer cell line', which three replicates per arm already establish without any machine learning.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use tumour gene activity to predict whether a liver metastasis grows by replacing liver tissue or by walling itself off.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on gene expression profiles of resected colorectal liver metastases, one profile per tumour. This paper supplies only 6 mouse cell-line samples; the human set it reanalyses (GSE151165) has 30 samples.
plain_idea.predict: The histopathological growth pattern, replacement versus encapsulated/desmoplastic, as scored by a pathologist on a stained tissue slide following the 2022 international consensus guidelines.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Growth pattern separates 5-year survival of roughly 44% from 73%, so liver surgeons and oncologists act on it; a molecular predictor could flag high-risk patients from a biopsy. But this paper contributes no data at the scale needed.

more_or_better_data.why: Our verified data is 6 mouse spheroid samples; the published image classifiers were trained on whole-slide image cohorts of resected patients spanning two decades at Erasmus MC.

confidence_score.why: Three replicates per arm cannot support per-prediction confidence estimates for anything.

models_beatable.why: A 2024 deep-learning classifier reporting 0.93 development and 0.95 external-validation area under the curve, plus a prospective clinical 'copilot' study, is an honestly evaluated field.

guaranteed_improvement.why: We cannot run the existing models as a baseline, we have no shared evaluation split, and our data is mouse cell line rather than patient slides, so every condition fails.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper's data. The scientifically interesting target, replacement versus encapsulated growth pattern of colorectal liver metastases, is not in any file the authors deposited; the deposit is a 3-versus-3 palmitate treatment experiment in one mouse cell line. A real project on this question would need a patient cohort with paired slides or transcriptomes and consensus growth-pattern scores, and that field already has deep-learning classifiers reporting ~0.95 external area under the curve.

effort.compute_note: Measured: the whole deposit is 1.2 MB gzipped and loads in under a second with pandas. Irrelevant, because there are only 6 examples.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the sample columns in GSE292820_rawCounts.txt.gz. I did: there are 6. That kills it in one minute.

verdict_reason: A5 killer, verified in the files: the paper's entire data deposit is 6 mouse cell-line RNA-seq samples (3 palmitate vs 3 vehicle), and A2 also fails because the prognostic label the paper is about, replacement versus encapsulated liver-metastasis growth pattern, appears in no deposited file. The human patient cohort with steatosis, growth-pattern and survival data is described only in a paywalled Nature article with no PubMed Central record and no supplementary deposit. The reanalysed public human set, GSE151165, has 30 samples and belongs to another study. Separately, the attractive task (classifying growth pattern) already has a 2024 deep-learning classifier reporting 0.93/0.95 area under the curve and a prospective clinical study.
